editorial.headline: Transformers Open Nationally, Blocked for Foreign Setup in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers transformer and rectifier manufacturing, open to all business scales nationally but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record’s moratorium flag.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27113 is an industrial manufacturing activity: the making of transformers, current converters, rectifiers, and their components or parts. In practical terms, the record places here the equipment that changes, distributes, regulates, or converts electrical power: distribution transformers, power transformers, special transformers, AC-to-DC current converters, radiators, commutators, electrical distribution transformers, arc-welding transformers, fluorescent or lighting ballasts, substation transformers for power distribution, and devices that regulate electrical transmission and distribution voltage.

That scope is broad but still coherent. It is not a general electrical-trading activity, and it is not merely installation or repair. The center of gravity is fabrication: producing the physical devices and parts that sit inside electricity networks, workshops, lighting systems, substations, and voltage-control environments. A founder reading this record should understand the activity as manufacturing for the electrical conversion and distribution chain, with both finished equipment and component-level production included in the field described by the Indonesian scope.

The scale position is unusually wide. The record marks the activity as open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so it is not reserved only for a large industrial investor in the national classification data supplied here. A smaller manufacturer making components, a medium-sized production operation, and a larger transformer or rectifier factory all sit within the stated scale envelope, provided the actual registered activity remains inside the manufacturing scope described above. Nationally, the PMA line is also clear: the activity is TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing recorded as 100 and the source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record allows a fully foreign-owned PMA structure for this activity.

Bali is where the answer changes. The same record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the Bali status as Blocked (risk class). The reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule supplied in the record is equally direct: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, with the source identified as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is this: the activity is open to foreign ownership nationally, but a foreign investor cannot register this KBLI as a PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, this transformer and rectifier manufacturing activity is foreign-open; in Bali, the record says it is blocked for PMA registration today.
